guard: a spawn or a resume may arm the event plane of the agent it names and no other, over both ACL fields and at every seam, and the wildcard form is deliberately left to ordinary ACL authority, and the remedy the refusal prints is the one that actually narrows
why: An event channel carries a session's tool inputs and outputs verbatim. On a static mesh there is
no ledger, so a caller-supplied allowSubscribe/allowPublish is attenuated by nothing at all, and a
resume document is admin-supplied JSON that re-arms a managed row which `renewManagedStaticCred`
then re-mints a credential out of at half TTL.
E1 removes the rule's predicate. E2 leaves the rule but narrows its INPUT to one of the two ACL
fields, which is the shape a refactor produces and which E1 cannot distinguish. E3 goes the other
way and makes the rule catch MORE than it claims to, which is the only way to show the
stated-limit cell is an assertion rather than a sentence. E4 removes the rule from the RESUME door
E5 swaps the resume door's actor half from the principal to the display name. A resume document
supplies both independently, so that mutant re-arms the victim's plane for a different principal while
E4's cell and every spawn cell stay green.
E6 is E2 on the OTHER door: the resume seam reads the read-set only and forgets the post-set.
E4 zeroes the whole list at once and so cannot see it, which is how the gap survived a review that
had already asked for the half-fence on the spawn side.
while leaving it on the spawn door, which is the state this PR was in when a security review found
it: every spawn cell stayed green and a foreign concrete channel was mintable through an inventory.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY. The suite imports the manager by relative source path (../src/manager.js), so
the mutated file is the file that runs and there is no build in the command. Its package-name
imports are core's eventChannel/eventChannelPrincipal, which the cells compare the manager
AGAINST; no mutation below replaces them, so a kill cannot come from moving both sides.
E7 rewords the refusal's own remedy back to the profile that ignores --allow-subscribe. Every
other cell stays green: the refusal still refuses, still names the channel, still releases the
name. Only the credential the printed command actually mints changes, which is the half an
operator pays for and the half no cell watched before.
E8 is E7 one field over: the printed CHANNEL rather than the printed profile. It exists because
the first version of section 9 graded the profile and then minted the suite's own channel, so a
refusal pointing an operator at a different plane would have kept every cell green.
E9 is the mesh-mode field: the helper picks ONE of the two routes off the mesh the manager is
actually running, and until now no cell watched that selector. E9 pins the selector open on the
user branch while the suite runs a STATIC mesh, so the refusal hands a static operator a
`cotal actor grant` against a ledger that does not exist. Every other cell stays green: it still
refuses, still names the channel, still releases the name.
E10 is E9's twin at the OTHER door, and it is a real defect rather than only an ungraded field.
The resume door selected the remedy off the resumed DOCUMENT's identity mode rather than off the
manager's. Those agree on an honest inventory and disagree on exactly the shape section 8 already
builds, a user-mode record under a static manager, where the refusal handed a static operator a
`cotal actor grant` for a mesh with no actor ledger to write it to. An engineering lens found it by
asking what E9 and R2 did NOT cover, which is the question a pair of mutants invites.

mutations.cell: a spawn asking for ANOTHER agent's event channel to READ is refused

mutations.name: E11 the single selector, inverted
mutations.expectRed: the refusal prints a mint command, naming a profile and a channel
mutations.cell: the refusal prints a mint command, naming a profile and a channel
mutations.note: After the fold there is exactly ONE mode expression for both doors, and this is it. The mutant reddens the spawn cell AND the resume cell in this suite, which is the point: a single selector cannot be wrong at one door and right at the other. The named cell is the spawn one. On the user mesh the opposite polarity is graded by R2 in the auth config. It exists because an engineering lens asked for the selector to be closed by construction rather than by assertion, and the fold is what made a single-selector mutant writable at all.
